title: Board of Registration in Pharmacy advisory on the sale of hypodermic syringes and needles
rule_summary: The Board of Registration in Pharmacy's Advisory on the Sale of Hypodermic Syringes and Needles (adopted December 6, 2016; the PDF listed among the Board's pharmacy practice resources is marked revised 12/14/21) informs licensees that M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 27 authorizes pharmacies to sell hypodermic syringes and needles to any person, of any age, without a prescription, and without identification; that the legislation does not limit the number or type of syringes and needles that may be sold to any one customer; and that no requirements or limitations exist to prevent a customer from acquiring hypodermic syringes and needles. As recommended action it states that the pharmacy should complete the sale of requested hypodermic syringes and/or needles without any further requirements or record keeping; that there is no need to restrict the quantity or type (e.g., IM syringes) of hypodermic syringes or needles that may be sold; that it is strongly recommended that the pharmacy stock single unit-of-use syringes for individual sale; and that pharmacies may provide information regarding proper use and disposal of needles and syringes.
exam_relevance: Tests the Board's reading of s. 27 - any person, of any age, without a prescription or identification, with no limit on number or type - and the difference between the advisory's recommended actions and a statutory requirement.

authority.name: Advisory: Sale of Hypodermic Syringes and Needles

common_confusions: The advisory's recommended actions are guidance: the pharmacy should complete the sale without further requirements, stocking single unit-of-use syringes is strongly recommended, and pharmacies may provide use and disposal information.

The advisory's permissive wording on use and disposal information does not restate M.G.L. c. 111, s. 25K, under which the Department's educational insert shall be provided to purchasers at the point of sale.
verification_notes: The Board's advisory read on 2026-09-16 both as the mass.gov advisory web page (adopted December 6, 2016; revised October 4, 2018) and as the PDF listed among the Board's pharmacy practice resources (revised 12/14/21); the two versions state the same content.
